name: Sandbox
description: What a Sandbox is built with, what one invocation leaves for the next, and what a run hands back.

scenarios.title: A Sandbox names the artifact it was built over
given: no Sandbox
scenarios.when: one is constructed with no `wasm_path:`
scenarios.then: it reports the bundled Guest Binary's path

scenarios.title: The caps a Sandbox was given are the caps it reports
given: no Sandbox
scenarios.when: one is constructed with each cap set
scenarios.then: each cap reader answers the value it was given

scenarios.title: The scheduling mode a Sandbox was given is the mode it reports
given: no Sandbox
scenarios.when: one is constructed with a scheduling mode
scenarios.then: its mode reader answers that mode

scenarios.title: Every cap has a value nobody has to supply
given: Sandbox options carrying no caps
scenarios.when: the caps are read
scenarios.then: each answers its default

scenarios.title: A cap set to nothing is a cap that does not bound
given: Sandbox options carrying `nil` for each cap
scenarios.when: the caps are read
scenarios.then: each answers `nil`

scenarios.title: A cap given a value keeps it
given: Sandbox options carrying a value for each cap
scenarios.when: the caps are read
scenarios.then: each answers the value it was given

scenarios.title: A whole-number deadline is still a deadline in seconds
given: Sandbox options carrying an Integer `timeout:`
scenarios.when: the timeout is read
scenarios.then: it answers the same quantity as a Float

scenarios.title: The memory budget is per invocation, not per Sandbox
given: a Sandbox whose memory cap is smaller than two allocations together
scenarios.when: two invocations each allocate within the cap in turn
scenarios.then: both complete

scenarios.title: Disabling a cap is not requesting its default
given: a Sandbox constructed with every cap set to `nil`
scenarios.when: an invocation runs past what the defaults would have allowed
scenarios.then: it completes

scenarios.title: A deadline reached is not a Sandbox spent
given: a Sandbox whose invocation was cut short by its deadline
scenarios.when: a later invocation evaluates ordinary guest source
scenarios.then: it answers its value

scenarios.title: A memory budget reached is not a Sandbox spent either
given: a Sandbox whose invocation was cut short by its memory budget
scenarios.when: a later invocation evaluates ordinary guest source
scenarios.then: it answers its value

scenarios.title: Setup is paid once and serves every run
given: a Sandbox with a Service bound before its first invocation
scenarios.when: several invocations in turn call that Service
scenarios.then: each reaches it

scenarios.title: What one evaluation writes to a guest global, the next cannot read
given: a Sandbox whose evaluation set a guest global
scenarios.when: a later evaluation reads that global at entry
scenarios.then: it reads nothing

scenarios.title: The entrypoint verb leaks no more than the evaluation verb
given: a Sandbox whose entrypoint run set a guest global
scenarios.when: a later entrypoint run reads that global at entry
scenarios.then: it reads nothing

scenarios.title: Interleaving the two verbs interleaves no state
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint
scenarios.when: evaluations and entrypoint runs alternate on it
scenarios.then: each observes only its own state

scenarios.title: Both frontends leave the same nothing behind
given: a scenario whose first invocation defines a global, a constant and a reopened core method
scenarios.when: both frontends run it and a second invocation reads all three
scenarios.then: they observe the same absences

scenarios.title: A failure is confined to the Sandbox that had it
given: one Sandbox whose invocation failed
scenarios.when: a separate Sandbox runs the same kind of work
scenarios.then: it completes

scenarios.title: The declared path set is fixed at the seal
given: a registry sealed with a set of bound paths
a path bound after the seal
scenarios.when: the declared path set is read
scenarios.then: the later path is absent from it

scenarios.title: Before the seal the set still grows
given: an unsealed registry
scenarios.when: a path is bound and the declared path set is read
scenarios.then: the new path is present in it

scenarios.title: The set is ordered by when each path was bound
given: a registry with several paths bound in turn
scenarios.when: the declared path set is read
scenarios.then: the paths appear in the order they were bound

scenarios.title: A Sandbox that binds nothing declares nothing
given: a registry with nothing bound
scenarios.when: the declared path set is read
scenarios.then: it is empty

scenarios.title: A run that wrote nothing carries nothing
given: a Sandbox
scenarios.when: an invocation that writes to neither channel completes
scenarios.then: both captures are empty

scenarios.title: What was written and what was returned are read separately
given: a Sandbox
scenarios.when: an invocation both writes output and returns a value
scenarios.then: the capture and the value are each readable in full

scenarios.title: Output past the cap is marked as cut, not silently short
given: a Sandbox with a standard-output cap
scenarios.when: an invocation writes past it
scenarios.then: the standard-output truncation predicate is true

scenarios.title: A truncation mark belongs to the run that earned it
given: a Sandbox whose invocation truncated its standard output
scenarios.when: a later invocation writes within the cap
scenarios.then: its truncation predicate is false

scenarios.title: A trap does not carry its output into the next run
given: a Sandbox whose invocation wrote output and then trapped
scenarios.when: a later invocation writes its own output
scenarios.then: the capture holds only what the later invocation wrote

scenarios.title: Each run's capture is its own
given: a Sandbox that has written output on an earlier invocation
scenarios.when: a later invocation writes different output
scenarios.then: the capture holds only what the later invocation wrote

scenarios.title: The error channel is a channel of its own
given: a Sandbox
scenarios.when: guest code writes to the error stream
scenarios.then: the bytes appear in the error capture

scenarios.title: A warning takes the error channel
given: a Sandbox
scenarios.when: guest code issues a warning
scenarios.then: the bytes appear in the error capture

scenarios.title: The guest may point its output stream at the other channel
given: a Sandbox whose guest code pointed its output stream at the error stream
scenarios.when: guest code writes to the output stream afterward
scenarios.then: the bytes appear in the error capture

scenarios.title: A redirected stream is redirected for one run only
given: a Sandbox whose invocation pointed its output stream elsewhere
scenarios.when: a later invocation writes to the output stream
scenarios.then: the bytes appear in the output capture

scenarios.title: The error channel is capped like the output channel
given: a Sandbox with an error-output cap
scenarios.when: an invocation writes past it
scenarios.then: the error truncation predicate is true

scenarios.title: An uncapped channel keeps what a capped one would have cut
given: a Sandbox whose standard-output cap is `nil`
scenarios.when: an invocation writes past what the default cap would have allowed
scenarios.then: the capture holds every byte written

scenarios.title: Both frontends separate the two channels the same way
given: a scenario writing to both channels
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same two captures

scenarios.title: Both frontends cut at the same place
given: a scenario writing past a channel's cap
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same capture and truncation mark

scenarios.title: A deadline does not take back what was already written
given: a Sandbox whose invocation wrote to standard output and then reached its deadline
scenarios.when: the capture is read off the raised error's Execution
scenarios.then: it holds what was written before the deadline

scenarios.title: The error channel survives a deadline too
given: a Sandbox whose invocation wrote to the error stream and then reached its deadline
scenarios.when: the capture is read off the raised error's Execution
scenarios.then: it holds what was written before the deadline

scenarios.title: A truncation mark survives a deadline
given: a Sandbox whose invocation truncated its output and then reached its deadline
scenarios.when: the truncation predicate is read off the raised error's Execution
scenarios.then: it is true

scenarios.title: A memory budget does not take back what was written either
given: a Sandbox whose invocation wrote to standard output and then exceeded its memory budget
scenarios.when: the capture is read off the raised error's Execution
scenarios.then: it holds what was written before the budget was reached

scenarios.title: The last expression is the answer
given: a Sandbox
scenarios.when: an evaluation whose last expression computes a value completes
scenarios.then: the invocation answers that value

scenarios.title: Both frontends carry the same values out of an evaluation
given: a scenario evaluating each shape the wire carries
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same values

scenarios.title: Both frontends carry the same values out of a Service
given: a scenario whose Service returns each shape the wire carries
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same values

scenarios.title: A value sent to the guest and returned comes back unchanged on both
given: a scenario passing each shape through the guest and back
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same values

scenarios.title: A value the wire cannot carry is refused the same way on both
given: a scenario whose evaluation returns a value with no wire representation
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they refuse it the same way

scenarios.title: An entrypoint is called and its answer comes back
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint that takes no arguments
scenarios.when: that entrypoint is run
scenarios.then: the invocation answers what the entrypoint returned

scenarios.title: Positional arguments reach the entrypoint
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint that reads its positional arguments
scenarios.when: that entrypoint is run with positional arguments
scenarios.then: the invocation answers a value computed from them

scenarios.title: Keyword arguments reach the entrypoint as a trailing Hash
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint that reads a trailing Hash
scenarios.when: that entrypoint is run with keyword arguments
scenarios.then: the invocation answers a value computed from them

scenarios.title: An entrypoint is named the same whether written as text or as a symbol
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint
scenarios.when: it is run with its name given as a String
scenarios.then: the invocation answers what the entrypoint returned

scenarios.title: Snippets are in place before the entrypoint is looked for
given: a Sandbox whose preloaded snippet defines the entrypoint
scenarios.when: that entrypoint is run
scenarios.then: the invocation answers what it returned

scenarios.title: Both frontends run an entrypoint the same way
given: a scenario running a preloaded entrypoint
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same value

scenarios.title: Preloading chains
given: a Sandbox before its first invocation
scenarios.when: a snippet is preloaded onto it
scenarios.then: the preload answers the Sandbox

scenarios.title: A preloaded snippet is there when the guest looks
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded snippet that defines a constant
scenarios.when: an evaluation names that constant
scenarios.then: it resolves

scenarios.title: A snippet replays for every invocation, not just the first
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded snippet that defines a constant
one invocation already completed
scenarios.when: a later evaluation names that constant
scenarios.then: it resolves

scenarios.title: Snippets replay in the order they were preloaded
given: a Sandbox carrying several preloaded snippets whose effects depend on that order
scenarios.when: an evaluation observes the result
scenarios.then: it reflects the order they were preloaded in

scenarios.title: Bytecode is a snippet as readily as source
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded bytecode snippet that defines a constant
scenarios.when: an evaluation names that constant
scenarios.then: it resolves

scenarios.title: A bytecode snippet replays for every invocation too
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded bytecode snippet
one invocation already completed
scenarios.when: a later evaluation names the constant it defines
scenarios.then: it resolves

scenarios.title: Bytecode without a name still carries its effects
given: a Sandbox carrying preloaded bytecode compiled without debug information
scenarios.when: an evaluation names the constant it defines
scenarios.then: it resolves

scenarios.title: A run reports the time it spent
given: a Sandbox
scenarios.when: an evaluation completes and its usage is read
scenarios.then: the wall time is above zero

scenarios.title: The entrypoint verb reports its time too
given: a Sandbox carrying a preloaded entrypoint
scenarios.when: that entrypoint runs and the usage is read
scenarios.then: the wall time is above zero

scenarios.title: A run reports the memory it took
given: a Sandbox
scenarios.when: an evaluation that allocates completes and its usage is read
scenarios.then: the memory peak is above the no-allocation baseline

scenarios.title: A run cut short still reports what it spent
given: a Sandbox whose invocation reached its deadline
scenarios.when: the usage is read off the raised error's Execution
scenarios.then: the wall time is above zero

scenarios.title: The reported peak never exceeds the budget that refused it
given: a Sandbox whose invocation exceeded its memory budget
scenarios.when: the usage is read off the raised error's Execution
scenarios.then: the memory peak is at or below the configured budget

scenarios.title: A run the guest failed still reports what it spent
given: a Sandbox whose invocation raised from guest code
scenarios.when: the usage is read off the raised error's Execution
scenarios.then: the wall time is above zero

scenarios.title: A run a Service failed still reports what it spent
given: a Sandbox whose invocation raised from a bound Service
scenarios.when: the usage is read off the raised error's Execution
scenarios.then: the wall time is above zero

scenarios.title: Both frontends report usage after a run that succeeded
given: a scenario whose invocation completes
scenarios.when: both frontends run it and read the usage
scenarios.then: both carry a usage record

scenarios.title: A run hands back one frozen object carrying everything it produced
given: a Sandbox
scenarios.when: an evaluation that writes output and returns a value completes
scenarios.then: the returned Execution is frozen and carries both

scenarios.title: A failed run hands the same object back through its error
given: a Sandbox whose invocation failed
scenarios.when: the raised error's Execution is read
scenarios.then: it carries the observables the failed run produced

scenarios.title: A value that is nothing and a run that failed are told apart
given: one Execution from a run whose value was legitimately nothing, and one from a failed run
scenarios.when: each is asked whether it failed
scenarios.then: only the failed one says so

scenarios.title: A trapped run says it failed
given: an Execution from a run cut short by a trap
scenarios.when: it is asked whether it failed
scenarios.then: it says so

scenarios.title: A failure before any run produces no Execution to carry
given: a Sandbox given an input refused before the guest runs
scenarios.when: the raised error is asked for its Execution
scenarios.then: there is none

text: A Sandbox is set up once and run many times, so the scenarios fall into what
construction fixes, what an invocation may not carry into the next, and what
a run hands back. The isolation half is witnessed on both verbs and on their
interleaving, because a mechanism that clears state on one entry and not the
Captures are read after failures as often as after successes, so the trap
paths carry their own scenarios rather than resting on the success ones. What
a run wrote before it was cut short is exactly what a Host App triaging the
Everything that raises — a rejected option, a snippet that will not compile,
an entrypoint that is not there, a cap reached — belongs to the error
taxonomy and is specified there. The registries behind preload and bind have
invariants of their own that no public surface shows; those are pinned by
unit tests and are not behaviors.
The guest-side output surface — how `IO` and the Kernel writers behave inside
the guest — belongs to the capability gem that implements it. What is here is
the host end: which channel bytes land in, where they stop, and what survives
